author: petertgiles
body:
## 👋 Introduction

This branch updates the debuggers for  VS Code launch file.  It fixes the Firefox and Jest debugging profiles.  I've been carrying these around in a stash for a while and figured others might find them useful.

### Features of both
 - Step-by-step execution
 - Stop on exceptions
 - Local variables, watches, and call stack

### Firefox features
 - Auto reload on changes - works great with Webpack watch mode

### Firefox limitations
- No debugging on packages.  I think something about the sourcemaps is not working.

### Jest limitations
- No debugging on packages.  This could probably be easily set up but I haven't had need of it yet.


## :warning:  Gotchas

The Firefox extension starts a temporary profile with no history or extensions by default.  I didn't find that very useful so I configured the extension to look for a special debug profile you need to set up.  Then you can persist your history and extensions when debugging.

By default the debugger stops on all uncaught exceptions and Urql usually throws one on startup so it may look like your browser hung.  I usually just uncheck the "Uncaught Exceptions" option and resume the debugging session.
![image](https://github.com/GCTC-NTGC/gc-digital-talent/assets/8978655/0a721b30-6432-4ef5-b8f7-64651fb522c6)

Sometimes if the browser window is started with a few tabs the debugger may not have attached the way you expect.  I usually close all but one tab then restart the debugger once or twice.
![image](https://github.com/GCTC-NTGC/gc-digital-talent/assets/8978655/f72a785b-6375-4c8c-8d63-e68d141bc651)

I didn't set up the Chrome debugger.  I'll let someone who wants it scratch that itch.  :laughing: 

I rarely find it useful to run the Jest debugger with the full suite of tests.  I'll usually specify the single file I'm interested in as shown in the commented out configuration line.

## 🧪 Testing

### Firefox
1. Setup the Firefox debug profile as shown in the launch file comments.
2. Install the Firefox debugging VS Code extension as prompted in VS Code when starting the debugger
3. Try setting a breakpoint and having the extension stop for you
4. Start webpack watch mode, update a file, see the browser automatically reload

### Jest
1. Find a test file and set a breakpoint
2. Specify the file path in the launch file placeholder line
3. Start the debugger and have the extension stop for you

## 📸 Screenshot

### Firefox
![image](https://github.com/GCTC-NTGC/gc-digital-talent/assets/8978655/9c1c3d47-f8aa-4a40-bf46-1cbfffeff007)

### Jest
![image](https://github.com/GCTC-NTGC/gc-digital-talent/assets/8978655/36ae878f-6df1-4fe3-94b7-48b0bd6cd9dd)

author: stebalien
body:
old: 4MiB/1024 blocks.
new: 64MiB/64Ki blocks.

This should work better with network-attached storage. My measurements indicate that we're writing less than 8MiB per epoch and around 4K blocks. Previously, that would have been ~4 writes, now it's always one write and we have room to grow.

fixes https://github.com/filecoin-project/ref-fvm/issues/1786

## Summary
Changes to accomodate the breaking changes in libcnb. 
 - updates bard from libcnb.poet to libcnb.log
 - updates Build/Detect to use the libcnb 2.x signatures with Funcs
 - updates to Build/Detect tests to meet the env requirements for libcnb 2.x
 - addition of Generate with tests for new Generate binary, modelled on Build/Detect
 - removal of deprecated methods that relied on function no longer within libcnb 2.x (mostly BOM stuff)
 - changes to tests to accommodate uninitialized log object resulting from libcnb.log using interface not struct.
 
Note that this **SHOULD NOT BE MERGED** until the go.mod change to use a local libcnb is reverted. 
The change is in place to allow development while there is no official libcnb 2.x release =)

## Use Cases
Allows for libpak to be used with extensions, and brings it up to the upcoming libcnb 2.x stream.

author: xuesichao
body:
**Issue #1856, #2674 :**

**Description of changes:**
According to `detect-library` the `detect()` could return browser info with the value of `version` being `null`. 

For example: https://github.com/DamonOehlman/detect-browser/blob/546e6f1348375d8a486f21da07b20717267f6c49/src/index.ts#L59-L65.
```
export class ReactNativeInfo
  implements DetectedInfo<'react-native', 'react-native', null, null> {
  public readonly type = 'react-native';
  public readonly name: 'react-native' = 'react-native';
  public readonly version: null = null;
  public readonly os: null = null;
}
```

In this case our `majorVersion()` will throw an error because it try execute `null.split('.')`. This change add a null check to avoid such case.

**Testing:**

*Can these tested using a demo application? Please provide reproducible step-by-step instructions.*
No. The change has been covered by unit test.

**Checklist:**

1. Have you successfully run `npm run build:release` locally?
Yes

No

This PR introduces a new concept in Cycle (and therefore our API). It is not yet released into production, so these API calls will not (currently) work outside of our development cluster. 

Global load balancers introduce the ability to do canary and/or rainbow deployments, and zero-downtime configurations. This is a huge new feature and one of our most requested.  They sit outside of any environment, and allow balancing between them. In the near future, Cycle will support deploying a 'new version' of an environment, and the global LB can balance traffic between them until such time that the old one is torn down.

… we've verified the funds are available first - not before

Deleting the state before the necessary funds are identified first results in funds disappearing without a recipient receiving them since the transaction then results in an error state being returned.  

This update defers the deleteState calls so that they do not occur if `partialBalance < neededAmount` is true (not enough funds available)

The ClusterRole definition was no longer up-to-date, with some incorrect permissions and some missing permissions. As a consequence, it could not be used to run some antctl commands, such as supportbundle.

We fix the permissions and modify the Antctl e2e tests so that they use a Kubeconfig file generated for the antctl ServiceAccount, instead of the admin Kubeconfig file. Hopefully, this will help keep the ClusterRole definition up-to-date in the future.

A few other improvements were implemented in that process:

* antctl now uses the typed SystemBundle K8s clientset, instead of a raw REST client. This helps define the correct RBAC permissions for antctl. Previous permissions were indeed incorrect as they used the "post" verb (instead of the "create" verb), which is only correct for non-resource endpoints.
* supportbundle unit tests now use an in-memory filesystem, to avoid writing test outputs to the local machine.
* the antctl ClusterRole is giving access to a few extra endpoints ("/metrics", "/debug/pprof/*") to increse the usefulness of the antctl proxy command.

Fixes #5136

author: bearfriend
body:
[DE53055](https://rally1.rallydev.com/#/?detail=/defect/698395690329&fdp=true): Fixer > User Tag List Items > Fix clearable functionality

Many consumers of `d2l-tag-list-item` and `TagListItemMixin` use custom (usually data) attributes on tags to identify them. This PR adds a `key` property to the `tag-list-item-mixin` to act as a unique identifier for each tag, and includes it in the `d2l-tag-list-item-clear` event (though I'm not sure how valuable it really is there since `e.target.key` is already available).

Sometimes there are additional attributes added to denote relationships to other objects/entities. This seems like a reasonable and appropriate practice to me that does not require facilitation through the component/mixin.

Additionally, and probably more importantly, I've added a `displayText` option to `_renderTag` which allows consumers to give the tag a simple label for use within various langterms and screenreader announcements. This is useful when the contents of the tag are [not a simple string](https://github.com/BrightspaceHypermediaComponents/users/blob/8b256864f75e52f1e491aa24aad8eabe149a11e5/components/user-tag-list-item.js#L97-L105).

The only place that uses `_renderTag` with non-string contents already doesn't announce or localize properly, so this should be updated to pass `displayText`, but it can be done at any time:
[BrightspaceHypermediaComponents/users](https://github.com/BrightspaceHypermediaComponents/users/blob/8b256864f75e52f1e491aa24aad8eabe149a11e5/components/user-tag-list-item.js#L113)

Changing the event `detail` is technically a breaking change, but nothing is actually using the existing `detail.value`, so these uses of `d2l-tag-list-item-clear` _can_ be updated to use `key` but are not required:
[Brightspace/insights-adoption-dashboard](https://github.com/Brightspace/insights-adoption-dashboard/blob/1fd2584624207e3b099fde9e91a7cbe3f264d8fc/components/tags-list.js#L173)
[Brightspace/d2l-outcomes](https://github.com/Brightspace/d2l-outcomes/blob/8fc3523234a7432e6b11a30aac453249903df88e/src/components/tags/activity-alignment-tag-list.js#L306)
[Brightspace/cds-reflection-tool](https://github.com/Brightspace/cds-reflection-tool/blob/0e99db37084fc5aad2fa24da17c3db97634121d1/src/reflection-tool-admin/components/admin-email-draft.js#L541)

`🤷` Weird things I kinda wish I didn't see:

# Releases
## braid-design-system@32.7.0

### Minor Changes

-   **Drawer, Dialog:** Support validation blocking closure of modal ([#1318](https://github.com/seek-oss/braid-design-system/pull/1318))

    To prevent a `Dialog` or `Drawer` from closing, e.g. due to validation, the `onClose` function can now return **false**.

    **EXAMPLE USAGE:**

    ```jsx
    <Drawer
      open={open}
      onClose={() => {
        const valid = runValidation();
        if (!valid) {
          return false;
        }

        setOpen(false);
      }}
    />
    ```

### Patch Changes

-   **TooltipRenderer:** Fix arrow overlapping tooltip corner radius ([#1316](https://github.com/seek-oss/braid-design-system/pull/1316))

    Fix for an edge case where the arrow on a small tooltip could the overlap the corner radius of the tooltip.

-   **Drawer:** Darken backdrop in dark mode ([#1316](https://github.com/seek-oss/braid-design-system/pull/1316))

    Increase the weight of the backdrop in dark mode to ensure the content is suffiently obscured.

-   **Drawer:** Fix entrance animation from `left` position ([#1316](https://github.com/seek-oss/braid-design-system/pull/1316))

    Apply the entrance animation correctly for a `Drawer` using the `left` position.
    Also reduced the horizontal overshoot for the transition for a smoother feel.

-   **Drawer:** Increase space between `title` and `description` on tablet ([#1316](https://github.com/seek-oss/braid-design-system/pull/1316))

-   **Drawer:** Align horizontal gutters with PageBlock ([#1316](https://github.com/seek-oss/braid-design-system/pull/1316))

    Given a `Drawer` is full width on a mobile device, applying the same horizontal gutter rules as `PageBlock` makes sense.
    This ensures content on a mobile will have the same available space whether its in the page, or inside a `Drawer`.

author: gmlueck
body:
Remove `errc_for` and `error_category_for`, which were underspecified.

I think `errc_for` was intended to be the type of an error code enumeration that each backends provides.  In fact, the spec used to say that each backend was required to define such an enumeration. However, the OpenCL backend interop spec does not do this, and we do not know of any backend that does.

I think `error_category_for` was supposed to return the static error category object for each backend, although the spec did not provide any explanation for this function.  Again, the OpenCL backend interop spec does not document any such object, and we do not know of any backend that does this.

Remove an example that used `error_category_for` for the OpenCL backend.  I do not think this example would work given the current state of the OpenCL backend interop spec.

The direction for backend specific errors seems to have moved in a different direction.  The OpenCL backend interop spec defines a free function `opencl::get_error_code`, which returns a backend specific error code from a SYCL `exception` object.  Other backends seem to be following this model.  With this model, there is no need for the core SYCL specification to mandate an error code enumeration or error category for each backend.

Addresses #164.

Addresses #3230

This PR replaces Pyro's use of `flake8` and `isort` with `ruff`, speeding up this phase of linting by about 200x.

**Before this PR**
```sh
$ time (flake8 ; isort --check .)
... 14.07s user 0.27s system 99% cpu 14.402 total
```
**After this PR**
```sh
$ time ruff check .
...  0.09s user 0.04s system 182% cpu 0.073 total
```

I've enabled only the most basic of ruff checks: E, F, and I.
